scopeMarkdown:
Everything the Tizen research (`/Users/dinko/work-private/projects/dXn/nsh/nsh-root/_projects/tizen`, 2026-10-26 to
2026-11-08) gives for implementation on route A (`tizen-web`) and route B on GPUI (`tizen`): G0-G4, A1-A2 and the
upstream step U, across four execution repositories. Nothing in the research has been run on a TV yet.

**Repositories.** `dXn.GpuiTizen` (this one: workspace, Tizen targets incl. aarch64, `xtask`, the gate, bindings,
diag app, the platform with platform-owned EGL, blob cache, partial presents and video, examples, host and packaging,
Lima VM, CI, store check, crates.io packaging, and every upstream PR preparation text under `docs/pr/`); `../gpui-fast` (changes 1-3, change 5
and partial redraws, video holes; `tizen` and `tizen-release`); `../wgpu` (EGL 1.4 fixes for issue #10708, GL program
binaries; `v30-tizen`); `../nsh/nsh-wt/tizen` (the NSH fork's worktree on `feat/tizen`, created at planning from
`origin/main`: core focus, TV keys and category, one wgpu, `Os::Tizen`, change 4, `nsh-platform-tizen`, video,
`nsh/tizen`, the `tizen` and `tizen-web` targets, fork CI). `../nsh/nsh-root` is read-only reference (the research
and the `upstream-pr/` format); the epic never writes there (owner, 2026-11-08).

**Owner-run sprints** (`s23`-`s25`, signed up for by the owner on 2026-11-08): SDK licence, certificates, pushes and
fork PRs, the emulator on KVM runners, TVs or Remote Test Lab, Seller Office submission, crates.io publication, and
opening upstream issues and PRs. Upstream merges and gpui-fast's release are the maintainers'; what they block gets the
owner's disposition.

**Not built, because the research does not give them for implementation:** route C (NUI views, the alternative to
B), the custom GLES renderer (the fallback if the gate fails, `d04-gate`), and the optional test setups (Raspberry Pi
4, the Windows emulator machine).

**Defaults the owner may change.** Scale 2.0. One host for this repository's apps (`lib/libdxn_app.so`,
`dxn_gpui_tizen_main`); NSH's is `libnsh.so` / `nsh_tizen_main`. Package ids `DxnGpuiTzD/C/L/V`. Key names of
`d14-keys`. Diag port 47123 over `sdb forward`. `tizen` built on the `v0.1.13` tag (`d05-gpui-fast-pin`). Voice Guide
assumed to follow AT-SPI focus. Renderer `Auto` (platform EGL, wgpu surface fallback). Video overlay by default.

**Gate.** If `s1` cannot build gpui-fast for 32-bit ARM for a reason no target or flag change fixes, work stops for
the owner's decision (`d04-gate`).

**Environment prerequisites.** `s1`: the pinned nightly. `s2`: NuGet for `Tizen.NET.Sdk`. `s3` (first link): the owner
installs the Tizen SDK CLI with the Tizen 8.0 common rootstraps (armv7, x86_64, aarch64) and accepts its licence.
`s4`: Bun, `upstream` in `../gpui-fast`. `s7`: Lima creates the `gpuitizen` VM. `s9`: `upstream` (gfx-rs) in
`../wgpu` with `v30`. NSH sprints: `upstream` fetched in the NSH fork (done at planning).
constraintsMarkdown:
- **No NSH in `dXn.GpuiTizen`.** No dependency on any `nsh-*` crate; NSH consumes it, not the reverse.
- **One gpui-fast for every crate.** `gpui-fast` and `gpui-fast-wgpu` are pinned exactly (`=0.1.13`, the version
  `nsh-platform-gpui` 0.4.0 asks for) and move only together with NSH's pin. gpui-fast changes reach builds only
  through `[patch.crates-io]` over all nine `gpui-fast-*` crates.
- **No desktop platform crates in a Tizen build**: neither `gpui-fast-platform` nor `gpui-fast-linux` (nor X11,
  xkbcommon or portal crates) in the dependency graph of any `target_vendor = "tizen"` build.
- **No C++** in any TV library. C code only through Tizen's public C APIs and the C dependencies of pure-Rust crates;
  the renderer and text stack stay pure Rust (wgpu, naga, cosmic-text); gpui-fast's `font-kit` feature stays off.
- **Documented native symbols only**: functions from the Tizen 8.0 common native API reference (Ecore, Ecore_Wl2 and
  Ecore_IMF under "EFL (Deprecated)" are allowed); never `tdm_client_*`, `tbm_*`, DALi C++, `dali-csharp-binder`
  (`CSharp_Dali_*`) or TizenFX's native libraries. EGL and GL ES are loaded at run time by wgpu (dlopen).
- **One export per TV library**: `dxn_gpui_tizen_main`, no exported weak symbols, `panic = "abort"`.
- **.NET stays out of the way**: one blittable P/Invoke in `Main`; no TizenFX or NUI; nothing per frame or per event
  crosses into C#; no callbacks from native threads into managed code; .NET 6 compatible (`DllImport`, not
  `LibraryImport`).
- **One full-screen, opaque window at the UI plane's size** (1920x1080 on every TV); no menus, dialogs, cursors or
  second windows.
- **The main thread stays responsive** (the TV's watchdog kills apps whose loop stops answering): no blocking work in
  lifecycle or Ecore callbacks.
- **gpui-fast's own rules** (with the documented API exceptions of change 5 and the video hole) (`../gpui-fast/AGENTS.md`, `docs/upstream-sync.md`): logic in `crates/<crate>/src/fast/`,
  upstream files only get one-line hooks, no new public API, controls are environment variables read in `fast/`,
  `script/check-upstream` passes; one branch per change, cut from upstream `main`, never stacked; never commit to
  the fork's `main`.
- **Owner authority**: the agent never pushes, opens pull requests, changes GitHub settings (Actions on the forks,
  secrets), creates certificates or accepts licences; those are the owner's steps in the owner-run sprints (`s23`-`s25`) or
  explicit go-aheads. Samsung certificates, `profiles.xml`, `.p12` files and Tizen rootstraps are never committed or
  redistributed.
- **Testing** follows `AGENTS.md`: each task adds its own selectable test group; sprint checks select only those
  groups; desktop-Linux runtime checks run in the `gpuitizen` Lima VM; raw logs and diagnostic reports go under the
  ignored `artifacts-temp/` (`artifacts-temp/agentx/tizen-gpui-platform/` for epic diagnostics).
- **Per-repository conventions.** `dXn.GpuiTizen`: MIT OR Apache-2.0, edition 2024, Conventional Commits. gpui-fast
  and wgpu: their own conventions (wgpu's `CHANGELOG.md` entries). NSH: `<area>: <What the change does>` subjects, never
  Conventional Commits prefixes, docs and `website/` (English and `zh-CN`) in the same commit, one test binary per
  crate (`tests/<name>/main.rs` with a module per area), no AgentX files in its branches, branches never rebased.
  No AI attribution anywhere.
- **NSH upstream rules** (`nsh-root/AGENTS.md`): one thing per PR, cut from upstream `main`; compat cases for new API;
  an issue before anything that changes a recorded meaning; nothing pushed upstream and no PR opened without the
  owner's go.

requirements.title: Workspace and repository rules
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The repository becomes a Rust workspace with the layout of `getting-started.md`, licensed and documented like the other dXn repositories.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
The root `Cargo.toml` is a workspace (resolver 2, edition 2024, `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, repository
`https://github.com/dXnSix/dXn.GpuiTizen`) whose members are `crates/dxn_gpui_tizen_sys`, `crates/dxn_gpui_tizen`,
`crates/dxn_gpui_tizen_diag`, `examples/counter` (package `example_counter`), `examples/long_list` (package
`example_long_list`), `examples/video` (package `example_video`, added with video) and `xtask`. `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE` and a `README.md` exist. `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
a dated nightly with `rust-src`, `rustfmt`, `clippy` and `llvm-tools`. `[workspace.dependencies]` pins `gpui-fast` and
`gpui-fast-wgpu` exactly (`=0.1.13`); the committed manifest has no `[patch]` entry pointing at a local path.
`[workspace.lints]` declares `unexpected_cfgs` with `check-cfg = ['cfg(target_vendor, values("tizen"))']`, denies
`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, and denies clippy's `undocumented_unsafe_blocks`, `dbg_macro` and `todo`.
`.cargo/config.toml` defines the `xtask` alias. Verified by the `policy::tests` group of `xtask`, which reads the
manifests and fails when a pin, a lint, the alias or the toolchain components drift.

`AGENTS.md` replaces its "no source yet" text with this repository's rules: what lives here and what does not (no NSH),
the validation commands, and the feature-oriented test layout: a feature's unit test group lives in
`crates/<crate>/src/<feature>/tests.rs` (module `<feature>::tests`) and is selected with
`cargo test -p <package> --lib <feature>::tests`; Linux-only integration tests live in `<package>/tests/<feature>.rs`
and run in the Lima VM through `scripts/lima-run.sh`; cross builds go through `cargo xtask cross`. `.gitignore` also
ignores the local rootstrap directory and generated TPK staging trees. A reviewer confirms the text matches the
workspace.

requirements.title: Tizen targets and the cross-build driver
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Rust's stock `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabi` uses software floating point; Tizen's `armv7l` is the soft-float ABI with VFP/NEON hardware (`toolchain-and-build.md`). Custom target specs with `vendor = "tizen"` give hardware floats and a cfg that tells Tizen from desktop Linux.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`targets/armv7-tizen-linux-gnueabi.json` (arch `arm`, `llvm-target` `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabi`, soft-float ABI
with hardware VFPv3 and NEON: features include `+v7`, `+thumb2`, `+vfp3` and `+neon` and exclude `+soft-float`;
`os = "linux"`, `env = "gnu"`, `vendor = "tizen"`, 32-bit pointers) and `targets/x86_64-tizen-linux-gnu.json` (the
emulator: x86_64, `os = "linux"`, `env = "gnu"`, `vendor = "tizen"`) exist and are accepted by the pinned nightly.
The `targets::tests` group of `xtask` parses both files and checks these fields, so a spec regenerated from rustc's
built-in targets cannot silently drop NEON or the vendor.

`cargo xtask cross --target <armv7|x86_64> [--release] [--clippy] [--check-symbols] -p <package>...` runs Cargo on
the pinned nightly with `-Zbuild-std=std,panic_abort` and `--target targets/<spec>.json`, sets the C compiler for
`cc`-built dependencies to clang with `--target=<triple>` and `--sysroot=<rootstrap>` (plus
`-march=armv7-a -mfloat-abi=softfp -mfpu=neon` on armv7), and links with clang and `lld` against the same sysroot.
The rootstrap path comes from `TIZEN_ROOTSTRAP_ARMV7` / `TIZEN_ROOTSTRAP_X86_64`, else from the Tizen SDK's default
location. A build whose packages need linking (a `cdylib`) fails before invoking Cargo with a message naming the
missing rootstrap and how to install it; an rlib-only build does not need one. `--clippy` runs `cargo clippy` with the
same settings and `-D warnings`. The `cross::tests` group checks the constructed command lines and environment for
both targets, including the missing-rootstrap failure.

Cargo selection flags pass through (`-p`, `--manifest-path` for another workspace such as NSH's `crates/gpui`,
`--features`, `--no-default-features`), `--all-tv-libs` selects every `cdylib` package of this workspace, and the
toolchain is always this repository's pinned nightly, whatever workspace is built.

**The 32-bit ARM gate.** `cargo xtask cross --target armv7 -p dxn_gpui_tizen` builds `dxn_gpui_tizen` (at this point
a skeleton whose Tizen-only dependencies are `gpui-fast =0.1.13` and `gpui-fast-wgpu =0.1.13`) with full code
generation for the armv7 Tizen target and exits 0; the same holds for `--target x86_64`. A failure caused by
gpui-fast, wgpu, naga, cosmic-text or another dependency on 32-bit ARM that no target or flag change fixes stops the
epic for the owner's decision (design `d04-gate`) instead of being worked around.

The workspace's release profile builds TV libraries with `panic = "abort"`, `opt-level = 3`, `lto = "fat"`,
`codegen-units = 1` and stripped symbols; the `policy::tests` group of `xtask` fails when any of these change.

Linking a TV library against a Tizen 8.0 rootstrap uses the Tizen SDK's GCC 9.2 toolchain (`NativeToolchain-Gcc-9.2`):
clang drives the link with `--ld-path=<toolchain>/<gcc triple>/bin/ld.bfd` (GNU ld: lld rejects the rootstraps' shared
libraries, which list imported symbols as LOCAL after `.dynsym`'s first global), `-B`/`-L<toolchain>/lib/gcc/<gcc
triple>/9.2.0` for the start files and `libgcc`, and `-L` for `libgcc_s` (`lib` on armv7, `lib64` on x86_64 and
aarch64). The toolchain comes from `TIZEN_GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<ARCH>`, else `<SDK>/tools/<arch>-gcc-9.2`; a linking build
without it fails before Cargo with install instructions. When the toolchain is installed, every build (gate,
clippy, linking) passes these arguments, so their rustflags match and switching causes no rebuild; without it, only
non-linking builds run, with the pinned toolchain's lld standing in. C code is
still compiled by clang. The `gcc::tests` group checks the arguments, lookup and failure for every target, and
`docs/setup.md` documents the SDK installation. This replaces `TGT-2`'s "links with clang and `lld`" for linking
builds.

requirements.title: Tizen C bindings and the native-symbol policy
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Samsung's watch store rejected flutter-tizen's library for undocumented imports and exported weak symbols; whether the TV store checks the same is unknown, so plan as if it does (`distribution.md`, "Native symbols").

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`dxn_gpui_tizen_sys` holds hand-written `extern "C"` declarations (types, callbacks and constants included) for the
Tizen functions the platform and the diagnostic app use, and nothing else: the app framework (`ui_app_main` with
`ui_app_lifecycle_callback_s`, `ui_app_exit`, `app_control_get_extra_data`, `app_get_cache_path`,
`app_get_resource_path`, `app_get_data_path`), Ecore's main loop (`ecore_main_loop_thread_safe_call_async`, timers,
event handlers), Ecore_Wl2 (display, window creation, geometry, alpha, show/hide, `wl_surface` and `wl_display`
access, frame callbacks, key grabs), Ecore_IMF (context, focus, input panel, preedit, commit and delete-surrounding
callbacks), `system_settings` (get and change callbacks) and `dlog_print`. Declarations go through one macro that also
records each symbol in a `DECLARED_SYMBOLS` list. Link directives (`#[link(name = ...)]`) apply only when
`target_vendor = "tizen"`, so the crate builds and its tests run on macOS.

`crates/dxn_gpui_tizen_sys/symbols.allow` lists every allowed Tizen symbol with the public API module it is documented
in. The `symbols::tests` group fails when a declared symbol is missing from the allowlist, when an allowlist entry is
no longer declared, or when any declared or allowed symbol starts with a forbidden prefix (`tdm_`, `tbm_`, `dali_`,
`CSharp_`, `elm_`).

`cargo xtask check-symbols <library.so>` (and the `--check-symbols` flag of `cargo xtask cross`) reads the library's
dynamic symbol table with `llvm-nm` from the toolchain's `llvm-tools` and fails unless it exports exactly one global
symbol (`dxn_gpui_tizen_main`, or the one named by `--entry`, such as NSH's `nsh_tizen_main`), has no weak exported symbols, and imports only symbols from `symbols.allow` plus glibc
(`libc`, `libm`, `libdl`, `libpthread`, `librt`, `ld-linux`), `libgcc_s` and the run-time loader. Each violation is
reported by name. The `symcheck::tests` group drives the checker with fixture `llvm-nm` outputs covering a clean
library, a second export, a weak export and an undocumented import.

requirements.title: C# host and TPK packaging
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Third parties ship .NET apps (`.tpk`) or web apps on Samsung TVs; native code arrives as a library loaded by a small C# app, as Flutter's does (`native-host-performance.md`, sections 1-2).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`host/` holds `Program.cs`, whose `Main` marshals `args` to UTF-8 `argv` (with an empty `argv[0]`) and makes one
`DllImport("libdxn_app.so", ExactSpelling = true)` call to `int dxn_gpui_tizen_main(int argc, IntPtr* argv)`,
returning its result; no TizenFX, no other P/Invoke and no managed callbacks. `Dxn.GpuiTizen.Host.csproj` uses
`Tizen.NET.Sdk`, targets `tizen80` (.NET 6, which also runs on the .NET 8 of 2026 TVs), sets `AllowUnsafeBlocks`,
builds Release without PDB and includes the staged library through `TizenTpkUserIncludeFiles`.
`dotnet build host/Dxn.GpuiTizen.Host.csproj -c Release` succeeds on the Mac.

`cargo xtask package --app <diag|counter|long_list> --target <armv7|x86_64> [--sign <profile>]` builds the app's
release `cdylib` through `cargo xtask cross`, then stages a TPK tree under `target/tpk/<app>-<target>/`:
`bin/` (the host DLL), `lib/libdxn_app.so` (the library, renamed), `res/`, `shared/res/icon.png`, and a generated
`tizen-manifest.xml` with `<ui-application type="dotnet">`, the app's 10-character package id and app id, API version
8.0, profile `tv-samsung`, metadata `http://tizen.org/metadata/prefer_dotnet_aot` = `true`, `multiple="false"` and the
`http://tizen.org/privilege/internet` privilege. Only with `--sign` does it run `tz pack -t tpk -s <profile>`;
without it, it stops after staging and says signing needs the owner's certificate profile. The `package::tests` group
checks the staged layout and the rendered manifest from fixtures, and rejects package ids that are not exactly 10
alphanumeric characters.

**Owner-run.** For the diagnostic app and both examples, a TPK signed with the owner's Samsung certificate profile
(distributor certificate listing the test TVs' DUIDs) installs with `sdb install` and launches into
`dxn_gpui_tizen_main` on the TV emulator and on a 2024-or-later Samsung TV or a Remote Test Lab TV. The verification
log records the device, Tizen version, CPU architecture (`sdb capability`) and the result.

requirements.title: Diagnostic app
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Built first, to answer the unknowns of `gpui-route.md` section 9 and `native-host-performance.md` sections 6 and 9 on each TV model, with its results sent over the network because retail TVs have no shell and no `dlog`.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`dxn_gpui_tizen_diag` collects a versioned JSON report: EGL (vendor, version, client and display extensions, with
`EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache`, `EGL_KHR_partial_update`, `EGL_EXT_buffer_age` and `EGL_KHR_swap_buffers_with_damage`
flagged), GL ES (version, renderer, vendor, extensions, `GL_MAX_VERTEX_SHADER_STORAGE_BLOCKS`, `GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`),
the CPU (`/proc/cpuinfo`, pointer width), memory (`/proc/self/smaps_rollup`, `/proc/meminfo`), the measured frame
interval, what `setpriority` and `sched_setattr` return, and launch-step timings from process start (entry,
`create` callback, window, EGL, wgpu adapter, device and surface, first present). EGL and GL ES are loaded at run
time, never linked. The `report::tests` group covers the parsers (cpuinfo, smaps_rollup, meminfo, extension lists)
with fixtures, the step timer, and the JSON round trip.

The diagnostic app's wgpu probe opens one full-screen Ecore_Wl2 window, creates a wgpu instance with only the GL
backend, a surface from the window's Wayland handles, an adapter and a device (WebGL2 downlevel limits when the
adapter lacks vertex storage buffers), configures a Fifo surface and presents a fixed number of frames. Each stage's
duration, or its failure with the stage name and error text, goes into the report; a failure never stops the report
from being served. The `probe::tests` group drives the stage sequence with a fake backend: success, a failure at each
stage, and the report contents in both cases.

The diagnostic app listens on TCP port 47123 (overridable through an `app_control` extra) and serves the latest report and its log lines to a client; `cargo xtask diag pull [--port

]` connects (through `sdb forward tcp:

tcp:

`), saves the report to `artifacts-temp/diag/-.json` and prints a one-screen summary (GL version, vertex storage blocks, the flagged EGL extensions, probe result, launch timings). The `transport::tests` group runs server and client over loopback, including a client connecting before the report is ready and a dropped connection.

The diagnostic `cdylib` links for both Tizen targets (`cargo xtask cross --target <armv7|x86_64> --release
--all-tv-libs --check-symbols`) and passes the symbol check of `SYS-3`; `cargo xtask tizen-deps --target <t>` (added
here) shows its graph holds one wgpu (the version gpui-fast-wgpu uses) and no GPUI crate.

**Owner-run.** Diagnostic reports are pulled from the TV emulator and from at least one 2024-or-later Samsung TV or
Remote Test Lab TV, saved under `artifacts-temp/diag/`, and their answers recorded in the verification log: 32- or
64-bit userspace, GL ES version, `GL_MAX_VERTEX_SHADER_STORAGE_BLOCKS`, the flagged EGL extensions, whether wgpu's
own EGL surface worked (and if not, which wgpu issue #10708 pattern), launch-step timings and memory.

requirements.title: gpui-fast renderer changes on the fork
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Changes 1-3 of `gpui-fast-changes.md`, each under gpui-fast's own rules so it could be offered upstream unchanged later, and the release workspace through which the TV build uses them.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Change 1, GL ES 3.0 devices** (branch `gles-instance-path`). `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/fast/gles.rs` decides, from the
adapter: `uses_instance_textures` (true for a GL adapter without `DownlevelFlags::VERTEX_STORAGE` or with
`max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage == 0`, and on wasm as before), `required_limits` (the WebGL2 downlevel limits,
within the adapter's, whenever instance textures are used) and `atlas_format` (`Rgba8Unorm` for every GL adapter).
The three places in `wgpu_context.rs` that tested `cfg(target_family = "wasm")` become one-line hooks into it, and the
chosen path is logged once at info level. The `fast::gles::tests::device` group checks the decisions over adapter
flags and limits (GL ES 3.0-like, GL ES 3.1 without vertex storage, Vulkan, wasm GL); the existing `webgl_*` tests stay
unchanged and passing.

**Change 2, GL on request** (branch `wgpu-backend-env`). `fast::gles::backends()` returns
`wgpu::Backends::from_env()` when `WGPU_BACKEND` is set and today's default (`VULKAN | GL`) otherwise;
`WgpuContext::instance()` calls it through a one-line hook. The `fast::gles::tests::backends` group checks the unset,
`gl` and `vulkan` cases.

**Change 3, a pipeline cache on disk** (branch `pipeline-cache`). `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/fast/pipeline_cache.rs`
requests `wgpu::Features::PIPELINE_CACHE` only when the adapter offers it, loads data from
`<dir>/<wgpu::util::pipeline_cache_key(adapter_info)>` where `<dir>` is `GPUI_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` or the platform's
cache directory, creates the cache with `fallback: true`, passes it to every pipeline the renderer creates, and writes
`get_data()` back once the pipelines exist through a temporary file renamed into place. Nothing is read or written
when the feature or the key is missing. The `fast::pipeline_cache::tests` group covers: a second start finds and uses
the file, corrupt data falls back without error, nothing is written without the feature, and the write is atomic.

Each change sits on its own branch cut from upstream `main` (`gles-instance-path`, `wgpu-backend-env`,
`pipeline-cache`), never stacked, with no new public API, logic only under `src/fast/` and one-line hooks in upstream
files. The integration branch `tizen` starts at the commit of gpui-fast's `v0.1.13` tag and cherry-picks the three
branches' commits and that of `wgpu-test-lints` (cut from upstream `main` like them: it fixes clippy errors already
present on upstream `main` in `gpui_wgpu`'s test targets, which upstream CI never lints); on it, `script/check-upstream` reports no violations and
`cargo clippy -p gpui_wgpu --all-targets --features test-support -- -D warnings` passes.

`cargo xtask gpui-fast-release` (in this repository) generates gpui-fast's release workspace from `../gpui-fast`'s
`tizen` branch with `bun script/prepare-release.ts --tag v0.1.13`, checks it with
`cargo check --manifest-path target/release-workspace/Cargo.toml --workspace --lib --all-features`, and commits
exactly that output (never edited by hand) to the fork's local `tizen-release` branch through a git worktree. With
`--verify` it commits nothing; it regenerates and checks the workspace, writes
`artifacts-temp/gpui-fast-patch.toml` (a Cargo config patching all nine `gpui-fast-*` crates with `path` entries into
the release workspace), runs `cargo tree -i gpui-fast` with that config, fails on a "patch was not used" warning for a
crate the Tizen graph uses (the desktop platform crates are never in it, so their patches stay unused by design) or
when the tree does not resolve `gpui-fast` to the release workspace, and prints `gpui-fast patch ok`. The
`release::tests` group checks the nine generated patch entries and the parsing of `cargo tree` output.

requirements.title: Platform logic, testable on the Mac
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The decisions of the Tizen platform for GPUI that do not need Tizen to run, kept apart from the Tizen shell so they are proven by host tests (design `d10-logic-shell-split`).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Dispatcher.** `dxn_gpui_tizen`'s dispatcher implements GPUI's `PlatformDispatcher` over a `MainLoop` abstraction
(on Tizen, `ecore_main_loop_thread_safe_call_async` and Ecore timers): runnables dispatched to the main thread from
any thread run on the main thread in FIFO order within each priority, high before low; `dispatch_after` fires no
earlier than its delay; background runnables run on a worker pool; `is_main_thread` is true only on the thread that
created the dispatcher (the one that runs `ui_app_main`). The `dispatcher::tests` group proves this with a fake main
loop: cross-thread posting, ordering, delays, and that nothing runs after shutdown.

**Frames.** A frame scheduler draws only when GPUI asked for a frame and the compositor's frame callback for the
previous frame has arrived (or none is pending), forces the first frame after window creation and after resume,
coalesces repeated requests into one frame, and never draws while paused. The `frame::tests` group covers each
case.

**Lifecycle.** A lifecycle state machine (created, resumed, paused, terminated) turns `ui_app_main`'s callbacks into
effects: pause stops frames and releases GPU resources, resume rebuilds them and forces a full redraw, terminate runs
GPUI's quit callbacks once; repeated or out-of-order callbacks (resume before the first pause, a second terminate)
produce no effects. `app_control` extras are exposed as a string map to the app. The `lifecycle::tests` group covers
the transitions, the ignored cases and the extras.

**Keys.** Ecore key events (key name, string, modifiers, repeat) map to GPUI keystrokes by the table of design
`d14-keys`: arrows, `Return`/`KP_Enter` to `enter`, `XF86Back` to `back`, `XF86Exit` to `exit`, the color keys,
media keys and channel keys to their documented names, digits and printable characters with `key_char`, repeats as
held keys; unknown key names pass through lowercased. The `keys::tests` group checks the whole table, modifiers and
repeat.

**Display and scale.** One display whose bounds are the UI plane's size reported by the window (1920x1080 by default);
the scale factor defaults to 2.0 and is overridden by `RunOptions::scale_factor`, then by the
`DXN_GPUI_TIZEN_SCALE` environment variable, accepting only values from 1.0 to 4.0; the refresh rate comes from the
measured frame-callback interval, 60 Hz until measured. The `display::tests` group covers the defaults, both
overrides, rejected values and logical sizes.

requirements.title: The Tizen platform spike and the examples
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: GPUI on an Ecore_Wl2 window, with wgpu drawing through its own EGL surface (`gpui-route.md`, sections 2-3), and plain GPUI apps that prove it before NSH comes into it.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`dxn_gpui_tizen::run(argc, argv, RunOptions, on_launch)` starts GPUI with `Application::with_platform` on a
`TizenPlatform` whose `Platform::run` enters `ui_app_main` and calls GPUI's finish-launching callback from the
`create` callback; `quit` calls `ui_app_exit`; before any renderer exists it sets `GPUI_PIPELINE_CACHE_DIR` to
`app_get_cache_path()`; menus, dialogs, cursors, screen capture and a second window are no-ops or errors; the
clipboard is in-process. For both Tizen targets, `cargo xtask tizen-deps --target <t>` finds no
`gpui-fast-platform`, `gpui-fast-linux`, `x11rb`, `xkbcommon` or portal crate in the graph of the platform, the
diagnostic app and the examples, and prints `no desktop platform crates`.

The Tizen window implements `PlatformWindow` on one full-screen, opaque Ecore_Wl2 window: raw-window-handle Wayland
handles (the `wl_display` of Ecore_Wl2's display and the window's `wl_surface`) for `gpui_wgpu::WgpuRenderer::new`,
`on_request_frame` driven by the frame scheduler of `CORE-2` from Ecore_Wl2 frame callbacks, key events through the
mapping of `CORE-4` into `PlatformInput`, bounds and scale from `CORE-5`, and the lifecycle effects of `CORE-3`
(pause: the renderer's surface unconfigured and its atlas cleared; resume: a new surface configured on the same
handles and a full redraw; design `d36-pause-unconfigure`). This
wgpu-owned surface stays the fallback path once the platform-owned EGL path of `EGL-1` exists.

`examples/counter` (two focusable buttons and a count; Left/Right move focus, Enter presses, Back quits) builds as a
`cdylib` exporting `dxn_gpui_tizen_main` on Tizen targets (calling `dxn_gpui_tizen::run`) and as a desktop binary on
other targets (through `gpui-fast-platform`, which is a dependency only for non-Tizen targets). The binary accepts
`--exit-after-frames <n>`. Its view logic is tested by its `view::tests` group with GPUI's test context, and its
library links for armv7 and x86_64 with `--check-symbols`, which also proves the shell of `SHELL-1` and `SHELL-2`
compiles and links.

`examples/long_list` (1,000 rows in a `uniform_list`; Up/Down move the selection and keep it visible, Back quits) has
the same two builds and `--exit-after-frames`, and its view logic is tested by its own `view::tests` group.

**GL ES 3.0 path on desktop Linux.** In the `gpuitizen` Lima VM (`scripts/lima/gpuitizen.yaml`, Ubuntu with Mesa,
Xvfb and the build dependencies), `scripts/lima-run.sh` runs each example's `gles_smoke` integration test, which starts
the desktop binary under Xvfb with `WGPU_BACKEND=gl`, `MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.0`, no storage buffers
(`MESA_EXTENSION_OVERRIDE=-GL_ARB_shader_storage_buffer_object`: wgpu 30 opens a desktop GL context through EGL
there, which the GL ES override does not reach), the local gpui-fast patch of
`GF-5` and `--exit-after-frames 60`, and asserts exit 0 and the change-1 log line that instance data goes through
textures.

Every TV library of the workspace (the diagnostic app and the examples) links for armv7 and x86_64 with
`--all-tv-libs --check-symbols` and passes the symbol check of `SYS-3`; staged TPKs exist for each example.

requirements.title: The platform completed: text input, keys, settings, fonts, accessibility
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Step G3 of `gpui-route.md` for this repository, accessibility included at the owner's request (2026-11-08).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Text input.** Each window owns an Ecore_IMF context. When GPUI's input handler reports an editable focus the
platform focuses the context and shows the on-screen keyboard, hides it on blur; preedit strings become marked text
with their cursor, commits replace the marked text (or insert at the selection), delete-surrounding deletes around the
cursor, and key events the IME consumes never reach the key mapping. The translation from IME events to
`PlatformInputHandler` calls is tested by the `ime::tests` group with a fake handler. `examples/long_list` gains a
filter text field above the list (an `EntityInputHandler`) that narrows the rows, tested by its `filter::tests`
group.

**Key grabs.** When the window is shown, the color keys, media keys and channel keys are grabbed with
`ecore_wl2_window_keygrab_set` (topmost) and released on hide and terminate; `RunOptions::grab_keys` can narrow the set;
`Return`, `XF86Exit` and `XF86Home` are never grabbed (Return's long press is Exit and force-terminates the app). The
`keygrab::tests` group checks the grab plan from options and the refusal of the forbidden keys.

**System settings.** `dxn_gpui_tizen::settings` exposes `SystemSettings` (BCP 47 locale such as `ko-KR` from
`ko_KR.UTF-8`, time zone, a font scale mapped monotonically from `system_settings`' font size with normal = 1.0,
screen reader on or off, and high contrast and reduce motion when the TV reports them, else `None`), read at start and
updated from `system_settings` change callbacks, delivered to subscribers on the main thread with bursts coalesced;
unsupported keys yield `None`, never an error. The `settings::tests` group covers parsing, the font-scale mapping,
unsupported keys and coalescing.

**Fonts.** The platform's text system is gpui_wgpu's cosmic-text system created without system fonts; it receives
only the families in `RunOptions::font_families` (default: the TV's UI family and its fallbacks) found in the font
directories of the fontconfig configuration (`/etc/fonts/fonts.conf`, its `<dir>` and `<include>` entries, `conf.d`),
falling back to `/usr/share/fonts`, read in Rust without linking fontconfig. The `fonts::tests` group resolves
directories and families from fixture configuration trees, including missing includes and absent families.

**Accessibility.** The window implements GPUI's `a11y_init`, `a11y_tree_update` and `a11y_update_window_bounds`
with an `accesskit_unix` adapter whose activation, action and deactivation handlers forward to GPUI's
`A11yCallbacks` on the main thread, and whose window bounds are the full-screen window at the origin in physical
pixels. The `a11y::tests` group covers the forwarding and the bounds; a Linux integration test, run in the Lima VM
under `dbus-run-session` with `at-spi2-core`, pushes a tree and reads node names and roles back over AT-SPI, and an
AT-SPI `DoAction` reaches GPUI's action callback.

The completed platform (text input, key grabs, settings, fonts and accessibility in the Tizen shell) still links into
every TV library for both Tizen targets with exactly one export, and `cargo xtask tizen-deps` still finds no desktop
platform crate.

**Owner-run.** On a TV, with Voice Guide on, focusing the examples' buttons and rows is read aloud. If it is not, the
verification log records what Voice Guide asked for over AT-SPI (for example Tizen's `GetNeighbor` or highlight
methods), and the missing Tizen extensions become a corrective task under finding-driven scope expansion.

requirements.title: Continuous integration
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Development on the Mac, CI on Linux: host tests, cross builds, the GL ES 3.0 path on Mesa, and the TV emulator on a runner with KVM (`gpui-route.md`, section 7).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` starts with a `plan` job built from AgentX's selectable-CI template
(`.github/actions/plan/`: `workflow_dispatch` inputs `jobs`, `platforms` and `grep`; `ci:<job>`, `ci:all` and
`ci-os:<platform>` pull-request labels; documentation-only changes run only `check`), then gates these jobs on it:
`check` (fmt, clippy on Linux and macOS), `test` (the host test groups), `host` (`dotnet build` of the host), `cross`
(armv7 and x86_64 builds with the rootstrap installed through the Tizen SDK's package manager in the job, then the
symbol check) and `gles` (both examples' `gles_smoke` tests under Xvfb with Mesa's llvmpipe) and `egl` (the platform-owned EGL path under
headless Weston); until `Cargo.toml` commits the forks' git `[patch.crates-io]` lines, every job that builds checks out
`dXnSix/gpui-fast` `tizen-release` and `dXnSix/wgpu` `v30-tizen` and writes the patch config with `cargo xtask
gpui-fast-release --from` (the platform needs the forks' API to build at all). `scripts/check_workflow_yaml.rb` reports `workflow yaml ok` for every workflow and the plan
action, and `.github/actions/plan/plan_test.sh` passes for manual, pull-request and schedule events.

`.github/workflows/tizen-emulator.yml` (manual dispatch and weekly schedule) runs on an Ubuntu runner with KVM: it
installs the Tizen SDK and the TV emulator image, boots the emulator headless, imports the signing profile from
repository secrets (`TIZEN_AUTHOR_P12`, `TIZEN_DISTRIBUTOR_P12`, their passwords and `TIZEN_PROFILES_XML`) only in
this job, packages and installs the x86_64 diagnostic TPK, launches it, pulls its report through `sdb forward` and
uploads the report and the emulator log as artifacts. The workflow passes `scripts/check_workflow_yaml.rb`.

**NSH fork CI.** On the `fork/tizen-ci` branch of the NSH fork, `.github/workflows/fork-tizen.yml` (fork-only, its own
file) cross-builds `nsh-platform-tizen` for armv7, x86_64 and aarch64 with the rootstrap installed in the job and runs
the symbol check, runs the TV-idiom specs under `nsh test --target gpui` and `nsh test --target tizen-web`, and has a
manual emulator job running `nsh test --target tizen` on a KVM runner; `.github/ci/paths.py --print` lists the new
crate. The workflow passes `check_workflow_yaml.rb`.

**Owner-run.** After the owner pushes, `dXn.GpuiTizen`'s `ci.yml` is green on GitHub for `main` (the `gles` job
included), the NSH fork's `fork-tizen.yml` is green on its fork PR, and one run each of `tizen-emulator.yml` and the
NSH emulator job either passes (a diagnostic report uploaded, `nsh test --target tizen` passing) or its failure (for
example the emulator not booting on the runner) is recorded in the verification log.

requirements.title: Owner-run publication and device acceptance
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: What only the owner's accounts and hardware can prove, in the final sprint the owner signed up for.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Owner-run.** The owner confirms GitHub Actions are off on `dXnSix/gpui-fast` and `dXnSix/wgpu`, then pushes the
gpui-fast branches (`gles-instance-path`, `wgpu-backend-env`, `pipeline-cache`, `scene-damage`, `external-target`,
`video-hole`, `tizen`, `tizen-release`) and the wgpu branches (`v30-egl14`, `v30-gles-program-binaries`,
`v30-tizen`); `dXn.GpuiTizen`'s root `Cargo.toml` and NSH's `crates/gpui/Cargo.toml` then get the git
`[patch.crates-io]` lines (nine gpui-fast crates on `tizen-release`, `wgpu-hal` on `v30-tizen`), `cargo tree` shows the
git sources, and the owner pushes `dXn.GpuiTizen` and the NSH `pr/*`, `feat/tizen` and `fork/tizen-ci` branches and
opens the fork PRs into the fork's `main` (merged with merge commits).

**Owner-run.** On the emulator and on a 2024-or-later TV (or Remote Test Lab), both examples render full screen at
1920x1080; arrows, Enter and Back work; the color and media keys arrive while grabbed; the long list scrolls by remote
and its filter field opens the on-screen keyboard and filters; leaving with Home and returning redraws correctly; a
changed system font size or language reaches `SystemSettings`. Results go in the verification log.

**Owner-run.** The verification log records, per device: the stripped library size, launch-to-first-frame time,
memory (PSS) after start and after scrolling the long list against the 300 / 380 MB budget, and frame times while
scrolling with key repeat, for both renderer paths (platform-owned EGL with partial presents, and wgpu's surface),
with the blob cache cold and warm.

**Owner-run.** The NSH counter runs with `nsh run --target tizen` on the emulator and on a TV with hot reload (an edit
on the Mac shows on the TV), and `nsh package --target tizen` makes a TPK that installs and starts.

**Owner-run.** The NSH gallery (`nsh package --target tizen`) on a TV is navigable by remote: D-pad focus through
every screen, Enter, Back with the exit confirmation on the first screen, color and media keys reaching the app, the
on-screen keyboard in its fields, and system settings (language, font size) applied.

**Owner-run.** First the loader probe `.wgt` (`TWEB-7`) on a TV, recording which of module scripts, import map,
iframe realm, CORS bootstrap and Wasm fetch work; then the gallery as a `tizen-web` `.wgt` runs on a TV, navigable by
remote, with start-up time and frame times recorded. If the probe fails, the documents' ways out (a hosted web app,
or a classic-script build of the app) become corrective tasks.

requirements.title: wgpu fork: EGL 1.4 drivers and GL program binaries
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The fixes for wgpu issue #10708 (a Mali GPU with EGL 1.4 on Wayland where wgpu's own surfaces fail three ways) and program binaries behind wgpu's GL pipeline cache (`gpui-route.md`, sections 4, 6 and 9), on `v30` branches of `dXnSix/wgpu` because gpui-fast 0.1.13 uses wgpu 30.0.1.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**EGL 1.4 displays** (branch `v30-egl14`, cut from upstream `v30`). On a Wayland window, when the EGL client version is
below 1.5, `wgpu-hal`'s GLES backend gets the display with `eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT(EGL_PLATFORM_WAYLAND_EXT, ...)`
when `EGL_EXT_platform_wayland` is offered, else with `eglGetDisplay` on the `wl_display` (as flutter-tizen and DALi
call it), instead of failing for want of `eglGetPlatformDisplay`. The choice is a pure function of the EGL version and
client extensions, covered by new unit tests in `wgpu-hal` (`gles::egl::tests::display_path`).

**Presentable configs and buffering** (same branch). Config selection on Linux Wayland accepts the presentable tier
that Android and OHOS already get, so a config without `EGL_NATIVE_RENDERABLE` can still present; window surfaces are
created with `EGL_BACK_BUFFER` where `EGL_SINGLE_BUFFER` is refused (the driver of issue #10708), retrying once with
`EGL_BACK_BUFFER` after a `BAD_ATTRIBUTE`/`BAD_MATCH` failure. Unit tests (`gles::egl::tests::config_tiers`,
`gles::egl::tests::render_buffer`) cover the tier ranking and the fallback with fake config attributes; on Mesa in the
`gpuitizen` Lima VM the existing GLES surface path still presents (one wgpu GPU test selected on the GL backend).

**Program binaries** (branch `v30-gles-program-binaries`, cut from `v30`). The GLES backend implements
`create_pipeline_cache` / `pipeline_cache_get_data`: when `GL_NUM_PROGRAM_BINARY_FORMATS > 0` (core in GL ES 3.0) it
keys each linked program by its shader sources and the adapter (`GL_RENDERER`, `GL_VERSION`), stores
`glGetProgramBinary` output, and on a later run loads it with `glProgramBinary`, falling back to compiling when the
driver rejects it; `Features::PIPELINE_CACHE` is reported for such adapters and `pipeline_cache_key` returns a key for
GL. A wgpu GPU test run on the GL backend in the Lima VM (Mesa supports program binaries) proves a second pipeline
created from the cache data skips compilation and draws the same pixels, and that corrupt data falls back.

The integration branch `v30-tizen` is upstream `v30` plus both branches merged; the version stays `30.0.x` so
`wgpu-core 30` accepts it. `cargo xtask gpui-fast-release --verify` also writes the `wgpu-hal` path patch into
`artifacts-temp/gpui-fast-patch.toml` (pointing at `../wgpu/wgpu-hal` on `v30-tizen`), and
`cargo tree -i wgpu-hal` for `dxn_gpui_tizen` on a Tizen target resolves to it with no unused-patch warning.

requirements.title: gpui-fast change 5 and partial redraws
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Drawing into a target the platform supplies, scene damage, and redrawing only what changed (`gpui-fast-changes.md`, change 5; `gpui-route.md`, section 6; gpui-fast PR #45, closed, had exact scene damage for macOS and Windows). Change 5 needs new public API in `gpui_wgpu`; in the fork it is a documented exception to gpui-fast's no-new-API rule, offered upstream with measurements.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Scene damage** (branch `scene-damage`, cut from upstream `main`). `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/fast/damage.rs` computes,
for consecutive scenes of a window, the device-pixel rectangles whose output can differ (primitives added, removed,
moved or changed, including layer and clip changes), merged into a bounded list, with a full-window result on resize,
scale or atlas loss; `GPUI_PARTIAL_REDRAW=0` forces full damage. The `fast::damage::tests` group covers unchanged
scenes (no damage), a changed quad, a moved sprite, a clip change, many small changes merged, and the forced full
case.

**Drawing into a supplied target** (branch `external-target`, cut from upstream `main`). `gpui_wgpu` gains, as the
fork's documented API exception, a way to build a renderer on a wgpu device and adapter the caller created (including
one from `wgpu_hal::gles::Adapter::new_external`) and to draw a frame into a texture view the caller supplies for that
frame, with an option to flip Y for a GL default framebuffer, without creating or presenting a `wgpu::Surface`.
`fast::external_target::tests` render a scene through `WgpuHeadlessRenderer`'s device into a caller-made texture and
compare pixels with the surface path, flipped and unflipped.

**Partial redraw into a preserved target** (on `external-target`, using `scene-damage`). Given the damage of `DMG-1`
and the target's age (how many frames ago its contents were drawn, 0 when unknown), the renderer loads the existing
contents and draws only inside the bounding rectangle of the union of the damage of the last `age` frames, scissored (a
conservative superset, design `d23-damage-external-target`: a render pass has one scissor rectangle); age 0 or more than the
kept history draws the whole frame. `fast::external_target::tests::partial` proves with pixel read-back that pixels
outside the damage keep the previous frame and pixels inside match a full redraw.

`scene-damage` and `external-target` pass gpui-fast's local checks on their own (`script/check-upstream` with the API
exception recorded in the fork's `docs/upstream-sync.md` exception list), are cherry-picked into `tizen` after
changes 1-3, and the release workspace regenerated by `cargo xtask gpui-fast-release --verify` still checks.

requirements.title: Platform-owned EGL, the driver's shader cache and partial presents
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: With a platform-owned EGL context the Tizen platform avoids wgpu's per-frame full-window copy, presents only damaged rectangles (as DALi does with `EGL_EXT_buffer_age`, `eglSetDamageRegionKHR` and `eglSwapBuffersWithDamageKHR`) and registers the driver's shader cache (`EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache`) before any program is compiled (`gpui-route.md`, section 6; `native-host-performance.md`, levers 4 and 5).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`dxn_gpui_tizen`'s `egl` module (compiled for every Linux so the Lima VM can test it) takes raw `wl_display` and
`wl_surface` pointers, loads `libEGL.so.1`, `libGLESv2.so.2` and `libwayland-egl.so.1` at run time, gets the display
with `eglGetDisplay` (or the platform variant the EGL version allows), chooses an opaque RGBA8888 window config (alpha
only while a video hole is active, `VID-3`), creates a GL ES 3 context and a `wl_egl_window` at the window's size,
hands the context to wgpu through `wgpu_hal::gles::Adapter::new_external` and `create_adapter_from_hal`, and builds
the renderer of `DMG-2` on it, drawing into the default framebuffer (`Texture::default_framebuffer`, Y flipped).

**The driver's shader cache.** When the display offers `EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache`, the `egl` module registers its
set/get callbacks before creating the context, backed by a `blob_cache` store: one file per key under
`<app cache dir>/egl-blob-cache/`, bounded total size with least-recently-used eviction, atomic writes, corrupt or
truncated entries ignored. The `blob_cache::tests` group covers store, load, eviction, corruption and concurrent
callers; the Lima integration test (`EGL-5`) shows the store registered on the display and reached through the
callbacks EGL was given; whether a driver calls them is checked on the TV in the owner's device run, where the
window logs the cache's counts to dlog (Mesa's llvmpipe advertises the extension but keeps its own disk cache).

**Partial presents.** Each frame the `egl` module queries `EGL_BUFFER_AGE_EXT` and passes the age to the `DMG-2`
renderer, which keeps the damage history and returns, before drawing, the frame's damage and the region it redraws
for that age, in GL's bottom-left coordinates (`DMG-3`). The pure `egl_damage` module (host-tested by
`egl_damage::tests`) reads the display's extensions and turns that into EGL calls: `eglSetDamageRegionKHR` with the
redraw region before drawing (`EGL_KHR_partial_update`), `eglSwapBuffersWithDamageKHR`/`EXT` with the frame damage
after, no swap when the renderer drew nothing, and age 0 (a full frame) without `EGL_EXT_buffer_age` or when the query
fails. Without the extensions it draws and swaps the full frame.

**Renderer selection.** `RunOptions::renderer` (`Auto`, `PlatformEgl`, `WgpuSurface`), overridden by
`DXN_GPUI_TIZEN_RENDERER`, picks the path; `Auto` uses the platform-owned EGL path when context creation and
`new_external` succeed and falls back to wgpu's own surface (`SHELL-2`) otherwise, logging the reason once. Pause and
resume release and rebuild the active path's resources (`CORE-3`). The `renderer_select::tests` group covers the
choice, the override and the fallback reasons.

**Desktop proof.** In the Lima VM, under `weston --backend=headless` with Mesa's software EGL on Wayland, the
`egl_wayland` integration test of `dxn_gpui_tizen` creates a `wl_surface` with `wayland-client`, runs the `egl`
module with a small GPUI-free scene through the `DMG-2` renderer, and asserts: the context is GL ES 3.x, the blob cache is
registered and its callbacks reach the store, a second frame with a small change swaps with damage (when Mesa reports buffer age), and read-back
pixels match the expected frame.

Both examples, built with the platform-owned EGL path, still link for every Tizen target with exactly one export, and
the symbol allowlist still holds (EGL, GL ES and wayland-egl stay run-time loaded).

requirements.title: Video
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Video through Tizen's player: on the TV's video plane under a transparent hole, and as textures GPUI composites (`native-backend-design.md`, "Video"; `gpui-route.md`, section 5). DRM and some advanced players need partner privileges; this epic uses only the public `capi-media-player` API.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Holes** (gpui-fast branch `video-hole`, cut from upstream `main`, a second documented API exception). GPUI can paint
a rounded rectangle that replaces the target's pixels with transparent black instead of blending, and the scene
reports whether the frame contains a hole. `fast::hole::tests` read back pixels through the headless renderer:
transparent inside the hole (corner radii respected), untouched outside, and later quads drawn above the hole blend
over it. Cherry-picked into `tizen`; the release workspace regenerated.

`dxn_gpui_tizen::video` wraps the public `capi-media-player` API: create, set URI, prepare asynchronously, play,
pause, stop, seek, volume, mute, looping, position, duration, completion, error and buffering callbacks (delivered on
the main thread), destroy. Its state machine (`video::tests`) rejects calls invalid in the player's state, serializes
asynchronous prepare and seek, and maps player errors to typed errors. Bindings and allowlist entries are added for
every player function used.

**Two outputs.** *Overlay*: the player renders to the TV's video plane through `player_set_display` with the overlay
type and the app's window (the display handle form the Tizen 8.0 public API accepts for a native window), positioned
at the video view's rectangle; while any overlay video is active the window switches to an alpha config and GPUI paints
a hole (`VID-1`) there, and switches back to opaque when the last one stops. *Texture*: decoded frames from
`player_set_media_packet_video_frame_decoded_cb` are converted (NV12 or I420 to RGBA) and uploaded to a `gpui_wgpu`
dynamic texture on the main thread, dropping frames when one is still pending. The conversion and the pending-frame
policy are host-tested (`video_frames::tests`); the output is chosen per player by the caller, overlay by default
where available.

**Owner-run.** On a TV and on the emulator, an example with a video view (`examples/video`: one clip, play/pause on
Enter, a focusable control row drawn over the video) plays an MP4 in both outputs; with the overlay, UI drawn over the
hole stays visible, and leaving the app pauses and releases the player. Results go in the verification log.

`examples/video` (package `example_video`) builds like the other examples (Tizen `cdylib` and desktop binary, with a
placeholder on desktop), plays its bundled clip on Tizen through `dxn_gpui_tizen::video` with a focusable control row
over it, has a `view::tests` group, and links for every Tizen target with one export.

requirements.title: aarch64 builds
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: 64-bit userspace on a retail TV is unconfirmed, but Seller Office takes multi-architecture packages and Tizen supports `aarch64` devices (`toolchain-and-build.md`, `distribution.md`).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`targets/aarch64-tizen-linux-gnu.json` (from `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` with `vendor = "tizen"`) is accepted by the
pinned nightly and checked by `targets::tests`; `cargo xtask cross --target aarch64` works with
`TIZEN_ROOTSTRAP_AARCH64`; the gate builds `dxn_gpui_tizen` for it.

The diagnostic app and every example link for `aarch64` with `--check-symbols`; `cargo xtask package --target aarch64`
stages an aarch64 TPK, and `cargo xtask package --app <app> --target all` stages one TPK per architecture plus the
multi-architecture `.zip` Seller Office accepts (layout per Samsung's multi-architecture packaging rules, checked by
`package::tests::multi_arch`).

requirements.title: Store readiness and submission
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A store-submittable app is step G4's exit criterion (`plan-and-risks.md`); Samsung's rules are in `distribution.md`.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`cargo xtask store-check <tpk or staged dir>` checks what can be checked before submission and prints a report:
manifest fields (package id, version, API version, `tv-samsung` profile, icon present and of the required size,
privileges limited to the declared list), exactly one export in the native library and only allowlisted imports
(`SYS-3`), library and package sizes, and the presence of the feature description file the submission needs
(`store/feature-description.<app>.md`, written for the app being submitted). `store_check::tests` cover a passing
package and each failure.

**Owner-run.** The owner registers in Seller Office, raises the native `.so` question with Samsung (`distribution.md`),
submits one app built by this epic (the NSH gallery as a `tizen` TPK, or the owner's choice) with its feature
description, and records the review outcome or its status in the verification log. It also builds the multi-architecture upload with `cargo xtask package --app <app> --target all --sign <profile>`, checks it with `cargo xtask store-check <zip>`, and records whether Seller Office accepts it, confirming or correcting the assumptions listed in `README.md` ("Packaging and store submission"): the CPU feature keys, the four-part manifest version, the `.zip` layout and where `tz pack` writes the signed package.

requirements.title: NSH: directional focus navigation in the core
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Every TV route needs D-pad focus; the TUI already has it in `crates/nsh-platform-tui/src/keyboard.rs`. Moved into `nsh-core`, it serves every backend (`nsh-integration.md`, section 7; `nsh-changes.md`, focus design notes). First upstream candidate.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`nsh_core::focus` (new module in `crates/nsh-core/src/focus.rs` or `focus/`) decides directional moves over plain data
every backend has: node id, frame in points, focus stop (`ViewProps::focus_stop`), input scope, covering layer or
modal, scroll ancestor and tree order. It reproduces the TUI's rules: Left/Right go to the nearest candidate in an
overlapping row, Up/Down to the nearest below/above with the overlapping column first, candidates are limited to the
newest visible modal and to layers not under a backdrop, a target outside its scroll ancestor yields a reveal delta
(`nsh_core::scroll::reveal_delta`), and focus returns to the recorded view when a layer closes. Its
`focus::tests` group covers each rule on frames in points.

The TUI is the first user: `keyboard.rs` builds the core's candidates from its mount (cells converted to points) and
takes moves, scopes, reveal and restore from `nsh_core::focus`, with no change in behavior: the TUI's existing
`focus_navigation`, `modal_focus`, `keyboard`, `popup` and `navigation` test modules pass unchanged.

**GPUI backend.** In `nsh-platform-gpui`, arrow keys (and the TV's arrows from the Tizen platform) move focus between
focus stops through `nsh_core::focus` over the backend's frames, Enter presses the focused pressable, the focused
view is revealed in its scroll views, `focus:` classes and `onFocus`/`onBlur` follow, and modals and popups scope
focus. A new test group in `nsh-platform-gpui` drives these with GPUI's test context.

**Pressables as focus stops on the desktops.** On macOS, Windows, Linux and GPUI, Tab and Shift+Tab also stop on
pressables (today only fields and native components), in tree order through `nsh_core::input::tab_stop`; arrows move
directionally as on GPUI. Proved by an app spec (`nsh test --target macos`, and `--target linux` in the Lima VM) and,
for Windows, by clippy for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` here and the fork's Windows CI in the owner sprint.

**What a TV adds.** Preferred and initial focus (`preferredFocus` / `autoFocus` props), focus groups (a `FocusGroup`
in `nsh/base` with `destinations` and `trap`), explicit `nextFocusUp/Down/Left/Right` overrides, and lists scrolled by
index when the next row is not mounted (the list scrolls with `scroll_to_index`, then focus lands on the row). The
existing focus API (`focus:` classes, `onFocus`/`onBlur`, `focusable`) keeps its meaning. Tested by new
`focus::tests::tv` cases in the core and a new `focus_group` module in `nsh-base`'s `base` test binary.

**Web runtime.** The browser runtime moves focus with the arrows over the frames it knows (DOM rectangles fed to the
core's decisions in Wasm), with the same scopes and reveal; a new browser test file covers it under `node --test`.

**Remote keys in tests.** `nsh/test` gains a remote-key step (`TestStep::PressRemoteKey`, `Driver::press_remote_key`,
a default in `agent::Native`, and a `remote(...)` method on the test module's keyboard) accepting the TV key names of
`TV-1`, implemented by the headless driver, the TUI, GPUI and web agents. A new `remote_keys` module in
`nsh-testing`'s test binary covers it.

Docs change with the code: `docs/dev/` pages for focus, the backends touched and testing, and the user-facing
`website/` pages in English and `zh-CN`; new props come with `tests/compat` cases. A reviewer confirms it.

requirements.title: NSH: TV keys, the TV category and one wgpu
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: What apps branch on is the TV, not Tizen: the same on Tizen native, Tizen web and Android TV (`nsh-integration.md`, section 6; `nsh-changes.md`).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`nsh_core::keymap::Key` gains `MediaPlayPause`, `MediaPlay`, `MediaPause`, `MediaStop`, `MediaRewind`,
`MediaFastForward`, `MediaNext`, `MediaPrevious`, `ColorRed`, `ColorGreen`, `ColorYellow`, `ColorBlue`, `ChannelUp`,
`ChannelDown` and `Info`, named in the `NAMED` table and mapped from the platforms that report them (Windows virtual
keys, Android key codes, the web's `KeyboardEvent.key` values and Tizen's web key codes, and the Tizen platform's key
names of design `d14-keys`); the TypeScript declarations list them. A new `keymap::tests::tv` group covers names and
mappings.

**The TV category.** `platform.tv` (true whenever the idiom is `Tv`, on any OS), a `tv={{...}}` prop group (QuickJS
renderer `dom.rs`, browser `dom.js`, host props, `TvProps` declarations) and a `tv` key in `platform.select`, looked
up after the OS's own key and before `desktop` / `mobile`; Rust gets `is_tv()` in `ambient`. Tests: new `tv` cases in
`nsh-js`'s environment tests, a `tv_props` module in `nsh-base`'s `base` binary, and a browser test file.

**The page sets the idiom.** The web player accepts `idiom: "tv"` (`nsh_environment` in `nsh-platform-web` maps it to
`Idiom::Tv`), so a `.wgt` page can tell the player it is on a TV instead of the pointer heuristic deciding. Covered by
a browser test.

**TV layouts on the Mac.** `nsh run` / `nsh dev` accept `--idiom tv` and `nsh.json` accepts a development setting for
it, for the desktop GPUI host and the web dev page, so 10-foot layouts and focus can be built on the Mac. A new
`dev_idiom` module in `nsh-cli`'s `cli` test binary covers parsing and what the hosts receive.

`platform.tv`, the `tv` prop group, the `tv` select key, the new keys and the TV focus props widen types: each has a
`tests/compat` case passing the v0.2.0 record with `cargo xtask compat`; if nsh-compat must learn to print them, the
nsh-compat change is prepared beside them (applied for the local compat run, sent upstream in the upstream sprint). `Os::Tizen`'s case belongs to `NTZ-2`.

**One wgpu.** `nsh-engine`'s `shader` feature moves to wgpu 30, the version gpui-fast 0.1.13 uses, so
`crates/gpui`'s lock holds one wgpu and shader views use the same GL device as GPUI on the TV; the engine's shader
tests pass and `cargo xtask tizen-deps --manifest-path <nsh>/crates/gpui/Cargo.toml --single wgpu` (from this
repository) finds one wgpu version.

requirements.title: NSH: the native Tizen backend
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: NSH's GPUI backend on `dxn_gpui_tizen`, built like the TUI and packaged like Android (`nsh-integration.md`, sections 3-4; `gpui-route.md`, section 5).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**The NSH half of the gate.** `nsh-platform-gpui` without default features builds for the armv7 Tizen target
(`cargo xtask cross --target armv7 --manifest-path <nsh>/crates/gpui/Cargo.toml -p nsh-platform-gpui
--no-default-features`, from this repository). A failure that is NSH's (not gpui-fast's) becomes the first task of
`s17-nsh-gpui-tizen`.

`Os::Tizen` (`name()` = `"tizen"`, `is_desktop()` false, `Idiom::desktop_on` false for it) in `nsh-core`, `"tizen"`
in the JS `OS` type, `platform.select({ tizen })` through the OS key; `tizen-web` keeps `Os::Web`. New `tizen` cases
in `platform::tests` and the JS environment tests. A `tests/compat` case (domain `tizen`, nsh-compat's `platform tizen`) passes with `cargo xtask compat`, the
nsh-compat change prepared as `TV-5` describes.

**gpui-fast change 4.** `gpui_platform` is an optional dependency of `nsh-platform-gpui` behind a default feature
(used only by `run_app`, the embed example and the headless text test, all gated), so the TV build has no
`gpui-fast-platform` or `gpui-fast-linux`; default builds are unchanged.

**A Tizen cfg in `nsh-platform-gpui`.** Under `target_vendor = "tizen"`, portal settings over D-Bus are replaced by
values set through `AppView`'s setters, the Linux UI and fallback font families by the TV's families, the X11
screenshot capture and the GTK web view are left out (web views report unsupported), and GStreamer video by the Tizen
video backend of `NTZ-7`. `cargo xtask tizen-deps` for the Tizen targets finds no `gtk`, `webkit2gtk`, `wry`,
`gstreamer`, `x11rb`, `gpui-fast-platform` or `gpui-fast-linux` in `nsh-platform-gpui`'s graph.

`crates/gpui/nsh-platform-tizen` (`cdylib` + `rlib`, library name `nsh`) exports one symbol, `nsh_tizen_main(argc,
argv)`, which runs `dxn_gpui_tizen::run` (as a git dependency pinned by `rev`, patched to `../../dXn.GpuiTizen` by an
uncommitted local Cargo config while both change), opens the full-screen window with `AppView`, loads the bundle from
the package's `res/`, feeds `dxn_gpui_tizen::settings` (locale, time zone, font scale, appearance, reduce motion) into
`AppView`'s setters as they change, maps the platform's key names to NSH keys (`TV-1`), makes Back NSH's back
navigation and, when nothing handles Back on the first screen, asks before exiting (Samsung's rule), and maps pause to
`Lifecycle::Background` and resume to `Active`. Its C# host (`host/`) is the same one-P/Invoke program, calling
`libnsh.so`'s `nsh_tizen_main`. Unit test groups in the crate cover key mapping, settings mapping and the Back policy.
The workspace's `[patch.crates-io]` carries the same nine gpui-fast lines (and `wgpu-hal`) as `dXn.GpuiTizen`.

**The `dev` variant.** With `--features dev`, the library connects the dev client to the dev server at a fixed local
port (mapped to the Mac by `sdb reverse`), falls back to listening for `sdb forward`, forwards logs and hot-reloads as
on Android. A unit test group covers the connection policy and the fallback.

**Video on Tizen.** `nsh-platform-gpui`'s video backend uses `dxn_gpui_tizen::video` on Tizen (overlay with a hole
for a video view without transforms or clipping, texture output otherwise), keeping NSH's own video controls; a unit
test group covers the output choice and the mapping of NSH's video commands and events.

**`nsh/tizen` (native half).** A `nsh/tizen` module with `isAvailable()`, product info (`system_info`), remote key
registration (through `dxn_gpui_tizen`'s key grabs), app exit, and Smart Hub preview where a public native API exists
(otherwise it reports unsupported natively and works on the web, `TWEB-4`), with TypeScript declarations; outside
Tizen `isAvailable()` is false and the calls reject. A unit test group covers availability and argument checks.

`nsh-platform-tizen` links as release and dev `cdylib`s for armv7, x86_64 and aarch64 with exactly one export,
`nsh_tizen_main` (`cargo xtask cross ... --check-symbols --entry nsh_tizen_main` from this repository), and the
symbol allowlist holds.

requirements.title: NSH: the `tizen` CLI target
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The normal workflow, as for the TUI (`nsh-integration.md`, sections 3 and 5).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`--target tizen` exists for `nsh run`, `nsh package` and `nsh test` (`run::Target`, `package::PackageTarget`), and
`nsh.json` accepts a `tizen` section (`package`: exactly 10 alphanumeric characters, `apiVersion`, `privileges`,
`signing`), shared with `tizen-web`, with errors for invalid values. A new `tizen` module in `nsh-cli`'s `cli` test
binary covers parsing and validation.

**Runtime and component.** NSH's `xtask` builds `runtime/tizen/release/` and `runtime/tizen/dev/`, each with the C#
host's `.dll` and `<arch>/libnsh.so` for `armv7l`, `aarch64` and `x86_64` (through this repository's cross driver),
and `dist` packs them; `nsh component add tizen` installs them (`COMPONENTS` entry, `runtime/tizen`), and the CLI adds
the component the first time a command needs it. Unit tests cover the layout and the component entry.

`HostPlatform::Tizen` in the dev protocol (older servers still read it as `Other`), with the CLI's install hint. A
protocol unit test covers both directions.

`nsh package --target tizen` writes a TPK from the release runtime: the host `.dll` in `bin/`, `lib/libnsh.so` for
the requested architecture (or one per architecture plus the multi-architecture `.zip`), the app's bundle and assets in
`res/`, the icon, and a `tizen-manifest.xml` generated from `nsh.json`, then signs it by running `tz pack -t tpk -s
<signing>` (or `tizen package`); without a profile it refuses with how to make one. Tests in the `tizen` CLI module
check the staged layout and the manifest.

`nsh run --target tizen` installs the dev TPK from `runtime/tizen/dev/` with `sdb install` once per device (and again
when the runtime changes), maps the dev port with `sdb reverse` (falling back to `sdb forward`), launches the app and
hot-reloads as on Android. The `sdb` command sequence is built by pure functions tested in the `tizen` CLI module.

**Apps with Rust crates.** The CLI generates `.nsh/rust/tizen`, a workspace of its own (as `.nsh/rust/gpui`): a
`cdylib` of `nsh-platform-tizen` and the app's crate exporting its UI sets as Android's `ui_sets!` does, with the
gpui-fast and wgpu-hal `[patch.crates-io]` lines in its root manifest, built for the requested architectures with the
Tizen target specs shipped in the `tizen` component. Tests compare the generated files with expected ones.

`nsh test --target tizen` runs specs against an app on a device or the emulator over the dev protocol (installed and
launched as `nsh run` does). Its driver setup is unit-tested; the run on the emulator is in the owner sprint
(`CI-3`).

Docs: a new `docs/dev/tizen.md` (both targets, what apps see, the CLI, testing, limits), the `nsh.json` table, and the
`website/` pages in English and `zh-CN`. A reviewer confirms it.

requirements.title: NSH: the `tizen-web` target
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Route A: NSH's web package as a Tizen web app (`web-app-route.md`).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`nsh package --target tizen-web` writes what `nsh package --target web` writes plus `config.xml` (application id and
package from `nsh.json`, `required_version`, the internet privilege, landscape, icon) and the TV shim loaded before
`nsh.js`, then signs with `tz pack -t wgt -s <signing>`. A new `tizen_web` module in the `cli` test binary checks the
package.

**The TV shim.** Back (key code 10009) reaches NSH's back navigation (the `BrowserBack` path); when nothing handles it
on the home screen the app shows its exit confirmation and calls
`tizen.application.getCurrentApplication().exit()`; color, media and channel keys are registered with
`tizen.tvinputdevice.registerKey` and delivered as the keys of `TV-1`; the player is created with `idiom: "tv"`. A
`node --test` file drives the shim with fake `tizen` globals.

**`scrollend` fallback.** On engines without `scrollend` (Chromium < 114, 2024 TVs), `nsh.js` ends browser-driven
scrolls after a quiet interval, so `onScrollEnd` and `onMomentumEnd` still fire; a browser test with `scrollend`
removed covers it.

**`nsh/tizen` (web half).** In a `.wgt`, `isAvailable()` is true and the module uses `tizen.*` and `webapis.*`
(product info, key registration, exit, `webapis.preview.setPreviewData` for Smart Hub preview); a `node --test` file
covers it with fakes.

`nsh run --target tizen-web` installs a dev `.wgt` whose page opens the dev server's page (internet privilege,
`<access>` to the Mac) and launches it; most development stays in Chrome on the Mac in the TV idiom (`TV-4`). Tests in
the `tizen_web` CLI module check the dev package.

`nsh test --target tizen-web` runs specs in headless Chromium with the TV shim and the TV idiom, as
`nsh test --target web` runs; the counter's spec passes that way.

**The loader probe.** `nsh package --target tizen-web --probe` writes a minimal signed-ready `.wgt` that tries, from
package files, a module script, an import map, a same-origin iframe realm, a classic bootstrap fetched with CORS, and
a Wasm `fetch`, and shows each result on screen. Its contents are checked by the `tizen_web` CLI tests; running it on
a TV is the first device check of `tizen-web` (`DEV-6`).

requirements.title: Upstream issues and pull requests
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Upstream, in the documents' order: NSH focus first, then TV keys and the TV category; the renderer changes to gpui-fast; the wgpu PRs; `dXn.GpuiTizen` on crates.io; then `Os::Tizen` and the Tizen targets in NSH; `tizen-web` packaging after the TV loader check (`nsh-integration.md`, section 8; `gpui-fast-changes.md`, section 3).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: For every NSH branch of this epic, `docs/pr/nsh/<area>/<topic>/` in this repository (in the format of `nsh-root/upstream-pr/`, which the epic never writes to) holds `README.md` (status, base, commits, checks, how to update and open it) and `PR.md` (title and body), each area has its `README.md` with the order, and the issues that must come first (focus navigation; TV keys and the TV category; `Os::Tizen` and the Tizen targets, raising that GPUI would be the native backend of packaged apps) are drafted there. Each branch is cut from `upstream/main` (or the previous branch of its area's stack) and holds only its topic's commits; its README lists the checks it must pass and the conflicts with the latest `upstream/main`, and says which checks have run, where (the integration branch `feat/tizen`, with every branch merged) and with what result. Rebasing a branch onto the latest `upstream/main` and running its checks on its own tip is the pre-open step of `UP-4`. A reviewer confirms it.

`docs/pr/gpui-fast/` in this repository (same folder format) holds the issue for `longbridge/gpui-fast` (the TV use, changes 1-3,
change 5 and the hole, what each touches, which add API and why, with the TV numbers of `DEV-3`, and whether they
prefer it in gpui-fast or Zed's GPUI) and one PR text per change branch; the branches stay cut from upstream `main`.
A reviewer confirms it.

`docs/pr/wgpu/` (same folder format) holds the PR texts for wgpu (the EGL 1.4 fixes on issue #10708, program binaries behind the GL
pipeline cache), and `../wgpu` has `egl14-wayland` and `gles-program-binaries` branches cut from upstream `trunk` with
the ported changes, their unit tests passing there (the command and result recorded in the PR text). A reviewer
confirms it.

**No TV needed; the agent prepares, the owner opens only gfx-rs/wgpu's.** Every upstream branch that needs no TV is made ready to open, in the order of `d33-upstream`: the NSH focus branches and issue; the TV keys and TV category branches and issue, with their nsh-compat companions; the one-wgpu branch; the six gpui-fast change branches and their issue; the two wgpu branches. Ready means: the branch holds only its topic's commits on the latest upstream base (NSH and nsh-compat: a fresh branch with the topic's own commits on the latest `upstream/main`, so no pushed fork branch is rebased or force-pushed; gpui-fast and wgpu: the change branch brought onto the latest `upstream/main` or `upstream/trunk`), it passes the checks its README lists on its own tip, it is pushed to the fork (`dXnSix/*`), and its PR folder records the base, the run, the push and the state "ready, not opened" with the text to paste. Nothing is opened or pushed at `longbridge/nsh`, `longbridge/nsh-compat` or `longbridge/gpui-fast`, no issue and no PR: the owner first makes an agreement with those projects' owners, outside this epic. The two gfx-rs/wgpu branches (`egl14-wayland`, `gles-program-binaries`) are made ready the same way, with their PR texts; the owner opens them after the TV run (`UP-5`).

**After the devices; the agent prepares, nothing is opened.** The same way as `UP-4`: the gpui-fast issue and PR texts get the `DEV-3` numbers and their branches are made ready again on the latest `upstream/main`; the NSH `Os::Tizen` and Tizen targets issue and branches, and the `tizen-web` branch after the TV loader check (`DEV-6`), are made ready, their folders saying what they wait for (gpui-fast releasing the changes and `dXn.GpuiTizen` on crates.io for the Tizen targets). Nothing is opened at `longbridge/*`; that waits for the owner's agreement with its owners, outside this epic. gfx-rs/wgpu: once the code has run on a real TV, the owner opens `egl14-wayland` and `gles-program-binaries` on their go, with the TV run in each PR's Testing section and the description and "LLM Use?" in their own words (wgpu's policy); each link and state goes into its PR folder.
